content.text:
I fixed it so the default `maxBodyLength` of `-1` now really means "unlimited", whether or not redirects are being followed. I haven't run any tests or a reproduction yet.

**Cause:** axios's default `maxBodyLength` is `-1`. In that case `lib/adapters/http.js` passed no `maxBodyLength` to `follow-redirects`, the library used for following redirects. That library then applied its own 10MB limit. With `maxRedirects: 0` that library isn't used, so there was no limit. Setting `-1` yourself didn't help either, because it took the same path.

**Fix:** when `maxBodyLength` is `-1` (or any negative value), the adapter now passes `Infinity` to `follow-redirects`. All four examples in the issue should now behave the same way: the 100MB body goes through unless you set a positive limit.

I also added a line to `README.md` saying the default is `-1` (unlimited), whatever `maxRedirects` is set to.

The issue also says this limit was never listed as a breaking change in the changelog. I didn't edit the changelog, since this fix brings back the original "no limit" behaviour.
